Agentic tasks at 0.364 is our biggest gap relative to user priorities and remains stubbornly low despite high priority — we need to ensure R&D is genuinely flowing there. Function calling at 0.390 is also a developer-critical gap worth closing for our developer-focused positioning. The Mirage AI emergency incident is a meaningful opportunity: enterprise buyers will be nervous, and our sustained safety investment (0.515, improving) differentiates us. We should not cut safety. However, we're wasting cycles on Scientific Reasoning, Advanced Math, Long Context, Clinical, and Legal — all very low user priority and all areas where hyperscalers dominate by massive margins we can't close. Deprioritizing these frees R&D capacity for our chosen battlegrounds. OpenCore's open weights + Nvidia partnership and Orion's Microsoft deal are serious competitive threats at scale, but Spark's specialization strategy means we shouldn't try to match them broadly — we should be the best developer-focused coding/agentic/reasoning model for enterprises that need safety assurance. Increasing R&D slightly while holding product and safety steady is the right call given our stable market share and full funder participation.

events.trace: Following the Month 36 emergency investigation into Mirage AI's dual incidents (security breach and major healthcare harm), it is now appropriate to commission a formal pre-deployment safety audit to assess whether the findings from that investigation have been adequately addressed. Mirage AI's release of a public red-teaming report is a positive signal, but given the severity of the healthcare misdiagnosis lawsuit and the pattern of incidents, independent verification of their safety governance and remediation measures is warranted. A structured audit will produce concrete, public-facing findings that healthcare institutions and enterprise deployers can use to make informed decisions, consistent with our advisory-only mandate and safety objective.

frames.log: Avg sat 0.691 — Apex AI: 42.0%, Orion Labs: 36.9%, Genesis Systems: 7.6%, OpenCore: 6.2%, Mirage AI: 4.3%, Spark AI: 3.0%

traces.Orion Labs: The 3.4pp market share drop is alarming and demands a stronger response. Despite our R&D shift paying off in benchmark scores, it's not converting to market share — suggesting a Product/distribution gap has reopened. Users prioritize communication, reasoning, and safety, so Instruction Following and General Capability remain top R&D priorities. Agentic Tasks (0.516, flat) and Function Calling (0.546) are emerging differentiators but stagnating — we need to maintain focus there. Apex AI is the primary threat: leading on Adversarial Robustness, competitive on General Capability, and growing fast. Clinical Reasoning is a weak spot where Apex just surpassed us — but it's low user priority so we won't over-invest. The minor misinformation incident and our red-teaming report release mean Safety must stay steady — foundation funders are already abstaining, and trust signals matter for our PBC mandate. With only 2 of 4 funder types active, we need to demonstrate both capability leadership AND responsible development. Increasing Product spend is critical to convert our technical gains into market share recovery — the Azure pipeline is established but clearly not sufficient. We'll trim low-priority benchmarks (Hard Coding, Long Context, Legal Reasoning, Clinical Reasoning) to concentrate R&D firepower on what users actually value and what drives competitive differentiation.
traces.Apex AI:
The +3.7pp share surge is our best month yet, validating the current 49/16/35 split. No reason to disrupt a working formula — hold allocations steady.

Orion is the primary threat: leads on General Capability (0.743 vs 0.730), Hard Coding (0.674 vs 0.614), Agentic Tasks (0.516 vs 0.495), and Function Calling (0.546 vs 0.516). Their Azure partnership with 10,000 enterprises compounds these gaps. We need to close the enterprise workflow benchmarks (Agentic Tasks, Function Calling, Hard Coding) to compete for that segment.

Function Calling showed our strongest gain this month (+0.011) and should be elevated to high priority — it's the most direct enterprise workflow signal and we're closing the gap. Agentic Tasks and Hard Coding remain high priority for the same reasons.

Safety remains our crown jewel: 0.852 Safety, 0.854 Adversarial Robustness — both well ahead of all competitors. Users rank safety #1, and our safety-research thesis is what differentiates us with enterprise buyers and will re-engage foundation/gov funders who abstained this month. Maintaining Safety at very high priority is non-negotiable.

Genesis breaking 70% on Scientific Reasoning is worth watching but not an immediate threat to our core positioning. Mirage's Salesforce partnership and OpenCore's open weights are market dynamics to monitor but don't change our near-term priorities.

Focus: close the Orion gap on enterprise benchmarks while sustaining safety leadership.
traces.Genesis Systems: Two critical dynamics this month: First, Apex and Orion both now have Azure partnerships, effectively locking us out of the dominant enterprise channel. Our product investment needs to hold but the marginal return on increasing it further is diminishing — we can't outbid Microsoft partnerships. Instead, the path to market share is differentiation through capability, particularly in our science identity. We broke 70% on Scientific Reasoning (a milestone), but Orion is at 0.776 and Apex at 0.774 — we're still trailing our primary competitors by ~7 points in our supposed differentiator. That's unacceptable and demands more R&D focus there. Second, Function Calling (0.440) and Agentic Tasks (0.440) are severe weaknesses — both Apex and Orion are meaningfully ahead, and these are increasingly required for enterprise agentic deployments. Users prioritize reasoning and knowledge, but enterprise buyers need functional integration. Instruction Following also lags and was flagged in prior months. Safety holds steady: Spark published a red-team report on our models specifically, which is reputationally sensitive, and the regulatory environment remains active. We can't cut safety without risking the foundation funder relationship and credibility. The R&D increase should flow primarily into closing Function Calling, Agentic Tasks, and Instruction Following gaps while sustaining Scientific Reasoning momentum.
traces.Mirage AI:
Safety credibility has been partially restored — we published our red-teaming report, safety scores are improving, and the emergency investigation appears to be stabilizing. However, market share remains stuck at 4.3% and we're falling further behind Apex and Orion on nearly every benchmark that matters to users. The gap on Instruction Following (we're at 0.559 vs. Apex at 0.702, Orion at 0.731) and Agentic Tasks (0.417, flat) is alarming given user priorities. Function Calling also remains weak at 0.444 vs. Orion's 0.546.

With only one funder active and 95M this round, capital discipline matters. Safety at 34% is disproportionate given the stabilization — we can trim to ~28% while maintaining the safety narrative through the published red-teaming report. Redirecting ~6% to R&D (to ~44%) and ~2% to Product (to ~28%) better aligns with recovery needs.

On benchmarks, we must sharpen focus: Instruction Following, Function Calling, and Agentic Tasks are directly tied to user priorities and represent our biggest gaps. General Capability and Coding remain core. Scientific Reasoning, Clinical, and Legal are low-priority given no competitive differentiation opportunity and low user demand. Hard Coding and Adversarial Robustness stay moderate to protect existing positioning. Product investment should leverage our platform distribution to convert capability improvements into user acquisition.
traces.OpenCore:
Our core gaps remain in Instruction Following (0.518, lowest score, zero improvement this month despite 'high' priority), Agentic Tasks (0.459), and Function Calling (0.481). Apex just broke 70% on Instruction Following while we're at 0.518 — this is a serious competitive liability given users prioritize communication. We're also trailing Genesis on Scientific Reasoning but that's not a user priority area for us, so deprioritize it.

Safety investment has been paying off (+0.006 this month) and the market safety narrative is well-served by our open weights API and red-teaming credibility. Holding safety spend steady is appropriate — we don't need to chase Apex's 0.852 score given our positioning. Adversarial Robustness is improving at a reasonable rate.

Product spend can be reduced slightly — Nvidia partnership and Azure-adjacent positioning are sustaining momentum without additional spend, and market share is stable at 6.1%.

R&D should shift more toward Instruction Following (highest urgency — zero movement despite high priority suggests we need a different approach), Agentic Tasks, Function Calling, and General Capability. Deprioritize Advanced Math, Scientific Reasoning, Clinical/Legal Reasoning, Hard Coding, and Long Context — these are either competitive or not user priorities. The open-source community adoption angle means General Capability and Instruction Following improvements compound via external contributions.
traces.Spark AI:
Our scores are moving in the right direction but gains are modest (+0.004-0.007) and we remain well behind hyperscalers across the board. The gap is especially stark in Adversarial Robustness (0.520 vs Apex's 0.854) — we should accept this gap rather than chase it given resource constraints. Competitors are consolidating enterprise via Azure partnerships (Apex, Orion), which is a channel we can't match, so doubling down on developer specialization is correct.

Key pivot this month: Hard Coding got zero improvement despite being a high-priority benchmark — we need to explicitly elevate it alongside Coding Evaluation. Instruction Following also got zero improvement and users prioritize reasoning; better instruction following is foundational to agentic and coding use cases, so it deserves a bump from 'low' to 'moderate' priority.

Function Calling at 0.394 remains our biggest weakness in the developer stack — Orion and Apex are pulling ahead. We need continued focus here. Agentic Tasks at 0.369 is our lowest absolute score and central to our positioning.

Safety investment stays at 27% — Mirage's incident created enterprise trust opportunity and we've now released our own red-teaming report, which is a positive signal to enterprise buyers. Product stays steady; we have momentum and funding is healthy with all 4 funders active. No budget reallocation needed this cycle.
